business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; ISO 3166-1 LU / LUX; Eurozone and Schengen member state of the European Union)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic with strong Napoleonic and German doctrinal influence; unitary national legal system; no tax or corporate law sub-state distinction; EU directives and regulations are directly applicable or transposed into domestic statutes)

Luxembourg–United Kingdom DTAA of 1967 as updated under the 2019 UK–Luxembourg Multi-Jurisdictional Protocol
Luxembourg–France DTAA of 1993 with subsequent amending protocols
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI, 2017 — Luxembourg deposit of ratification effective 2019)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — freedom of establishment, free movement of services and capital
EU Council Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4th AML Directive), Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5th AML Directive) and Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (6th AML Directive in transposition)
EU Regulation 2023/1113 on information accompanying transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets (Travel Rule)
Benelux Union Convention and the bilateral Luxembourg–Belgium and Luxembourg–Netherlands conventions on taxation of income and capital
EU–US Data Privacy Framework (Executive Order 14086, 2023 adequacy decision) applicable to US payment processors acting as data importers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 April 2024 and aligned with CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 2021 (beneficial owners of certain legal arrangements); Law of 19 December 2020 on restrictive measures (financial sanctions); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; Commercial Code Book I and Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade and companies register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin or Luxembourg notary upon presentation of the original

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy certified and covered by Apostille or Consular Legalization as required by the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate shareholder piercing bundle: certificate of incorporation, register of directors, UBO declaration, certificate of good standing and ownership chain chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry, commercial court or tax authority of the intermediate parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization if outside the EU/EEA; official certified extract from EU national company registers may be accepted without Apostille under the EU Single Digital Gateway

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories against (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) restrictive measures implemented by the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, Defence, Development Cooperation and Foreign Trade, and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), and (iv) the PEP definition in Article 3(9) of the Law of 12 November 2004 as amended, applying enhanced due diligence to PEPs, family members and close associates; although OFAC and the FATF listings are not directly binding in Luxembourg law, the applicant's exposure to USD-denominated Mastercard and Visa rails makes parallel OFAC/SDN and FATF grey-list screening a mandatory market standard; enhanced due diligence is compulsory for the High_Risk_Special_License business model; negative media and AML intelligence checks via commercial databases (World-Check, Dow Jones, OpenSanctions) are applied by the Luxembourg registered agent; source of funds and source of wealth investigation is required for every 25%+ UBO and for any non-EU shareholder.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); official portal: www.lbr.lu (guichet unique for company formation, name reservation and publication)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin alphabet script; French, German, Luxembourgish or English names are admissible; non-Latin named entities require a full transliteration and, where applicable, a certified translation; the articles of association are drafted in French as the authoritative text, with Austrian/German or English versions permitted; every SARL name must be preceded or followed by 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' pursuant to Article 260 of the Law of 10 August 1915; the RCS applies an accent-insensitive search index and a distinctive-uniqueness test ('clairement distincte et ne prête pas à confusion') against the entire trade and companies register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking — requires prior CSSF banking licence authorization
Assurance / Insurance / Reinsurance — requires Commissariat aux Assurances authorization
Établissement de monnaie électronique / Electronic Money Institution — requires CSSF e-money licence under PSD2
Payment Institution / Payment Services / Digital Payment — requires CSSF payment services licence under PSD2
Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SICAR / RAIF / SIF — requires CSSF fund authorization or registration
État / State / National / Public — misleading state implication, prohibited unless ministerial authorization obtained
Luxembourg / Grand-Duché / Le Gouvernement — as primary distinctive element requires prior authorization of the Ministry of the Economy
Chambre de Commerce / Bourse / Stock Exchange / Clearing House — protected institutional expressions
European Union / EU / Europe / Global — potentially misleading supranational connotation; subject to refusal

Virtual Card / Card Issuer / Spend Management / Pay — sensitive tokens; not statutorily prohibited but will trigger pre-approval review by the RCS with a request to document the CSSF regulatory comfort letter before registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative name finding, the RCS issues a written refusal notice; the applicant may file a recours gracieux (administrative review) with the RCS Registrar within 15 days, and, if confirmed, a judicial recours en annulation before the Tribunal administratif de Luxembourg within 3 months of notification; an appellate remedy lies before the Cour administrative within 3 months of the first-instance judgment; commercially, the applicant may simultaneously re-submit an amended distinctive name (new non-confusion certificate) through the LBR portal; for sensitive or regulated tokens, written preliminary approval from the CSSF or the Ministry of the Economy supersedes the RCS prohibition and must be attached to the re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-office-only address is not acceptable for a B2B virtual card issuing fintech classified as High_Risk_Special_License; the CSSF and the Luxembourg notary require a genuine registered office (siège réel) in Luxembourg with administrative substance, local management access and full books-and-records availability; during the pre-incorporation phase, a domiciliation agreement with an authorized corporate service provider (CSP) at a physical Luxembourg address is permissible provided the true business address is declared to the RCS and the CSSF comfort letter process is initiated; a pure 'virtual' mailbox without physical presence or local management capacity would constitute non-compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915, the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ≈ 90% likelihood of announced and unannounced on-site inspection once any payment services, e-money or PFS authorization application is lodged with the CSSF; current CSSF supervisory practice, under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and Article 34 of the amended 2004 AML Law, includes periodic AML/CFT inspections with short notice; the FIU and the ITM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) may conduct coordinated checks; during the strictly pre-incorporation stage with a CSP domiciliation, unannounced physical inspection likelihood is < 10%; however, the high-risk card issuing classification makes earlier compliance verification visits by the registered agent and the notary probable (≈ 40%).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Title VII on the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL), Articles 710-1 to 710-26 as amended by the Law of 23 August 2023 (in force since 12 December 2023); complemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2003; electronic filing regime under the Law of 2 September 2011 on eJustice and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice through the eJustice single-window portal at www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif), executed before a Luxembourg notary and transmitted electronically to the RCS via eJustice, followed by mandatory publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000.00 minimum share capital for a SARL under Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 (as amended by the Law of 23 August 2023, in force 12 December 2023). The capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation and deposited in a blocked subscription account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the company in formation with a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank issues a blocking certificate to the notary, and the funds are automatically released only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.À R.L. 1. Share Subscription: The subscriber confirms subscription of 12,000 shares of EUR 1.00 nominal value, fully paid in cash; allotment approved. 2. Registered Office: Adopted at [Registered Office Address, L-#### Luxembourg]; management authorised to file and maintain the RCS record. 3. Officers: [Gérant A] and [Gérant B] appointed gérants (managers) with joint signatory powers within the corporate purpose. 4. Banking: Gérants authorised to open corporate accounts and to release blocked capital upon RCS registration. 5. Ratification: All pre-incorporation acts performed for the company are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-selection and Reservation with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / eJustice portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an eJustice/LBR user account. Submit up to three proposed corporate names in the form '[Name] S.à r.l.' and verify distinctiveness against the existing RCS register. Ensure the name does not contain restricted words such as 'bank' or 'payment' without appropriate authorisation and that the chosen name is compatible with the corporate purpose of virtual card issuance. LBR reserves the approved name for a fixed period, ordinarily four months, pending the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name variants (minimum three)
Identification particulars of each incorporating shareholder
Confirmation that the corporate purpose uses ISIC 6619 and permits regulated payment/card activities
eJustice/LBR account activation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on grounds of identity, similarity, or public-order sensitivity, submit amended name variants promptly. The RCS registrar must provide a reasoned decision which may be challenged by administrative appeal; alternatively, recomplete the reservation request with consent letters from any owner of a confusingly similar name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the promoters, acting under the supervision of the appointed Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked subscription account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation at a Luxembourg-licensed bank. Wire or deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum share capital in cash. Obtain a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, declaring that the funds are held irrevocably for the company in formation and will be released only upon RCS registration. The account title, the names of the subscribers, and the nominal value of the shares must exactly match the draft articles of association.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC and account-opening application forms
Passport or EU national identity card of each shareholder and beneficial owner
Declaration of source of funds and source of wealth
Draft articles of association
Business plan and activity description covering virtual card issuance and spend management (ISIC 6619)
Notary-provided blocked capital certificate template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC or AML queries, cure by submitting enhanced source-of-funds evidence or a sworn declaration, per the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004. If the initial bank refuses the account, engage an alternative Luxembourg credit institution. The notary may accept a blocking certificate from any EU/EEA credit institution, provided a Luxembourg account remains available for the automatic release mechanism.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire public) in the district of Luxembourg; Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary finalises the articles of association (statuts) in French; verifies the legality of the corporate purpose; confirms the fully paid share capital and the blocking certificate; and verifies the identity, legal capacity, and signatures of the subscribers. The incorporation deed is executed before the notary, who retains the official minute. The deed records the corporate purpose of hosting, issuing, and controlling corporate virtual cards on Mastercard and Visa Direct networks and any ancillary spend-management services. The gérants' acceptance of office is recorded in the same deed or by a separate notarised or authenticated instrument.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the articles of association
Bank blocking certificate for the EUR 12,000 minimum capital
Identity documents and, where applicable, powers of attorney of the subscribers
Criminal record certificates (casier judiciaire) of the proposed gérants
Name reservation confirmation issued by LBR
Signed landlord consent or lease declaration for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any formal or substantive defect in the incorporation deed may be remedied by a rectificatory notarial deed executed before the incorporation is registered. Where a defect affects the consent of a subscriber, obtain a fresh shareholder resolution and re-execute the affected clauses. The notary remains responsible for correcting clerical errors before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Statutory Filing, Registration, and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the eJustice single-window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the executed deed and all annexed particulars electronically to the RCS within the statutory filing period. LBR conducts the legality review under Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915. Upon acceptance, the company is registered, assigned its RCS registration number, and a corporate legal-entity identifier is obtained. The deed and registered particulars are published in the RESA, producing legal effect against third parties from publication.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (electronic certified copy)
Blocked capital certificate from the bank
Articles of association and all annexes
Identity documents and acceptance statements of the gérants
LBR name reservation confirmation
Statement of the registered office address and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for supplementary information (demande de complément d'information), the notary submits the requested exhibits through eJustice within the granted deadline. A refusal may be challenged before the Tribunal d'arrondissement of Luxembourg, and a corrected filing may be reprocessed once the notary has cured the formal defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Social Security Registration (AEDT, ACD, and CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); single-window coordination via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the company obtains its Luxembourg VAT identification number for the issuance of card-related fees and spend-management services; registers its corporate tax file with the ACD; and registers as an employer with the CCSS, including the gérants where they are assimilated to employees under Luxembourg social-security rules. The single-window transfers basic registry data, but active enrolment for VAT and employer obligations is mandatory within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract or certificate
Notarial deed of incorporation
Identification particulars of the gérants and shareholders
Projected annual turnover estimate for VAT registration threshold analysis
Manager or employment contracts where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration before the AEDT or CCSS may trigger a fine or penalty surcharge. Submit an explanatory letter requesting waiver or reduction of the penalty, accompanied by proof of RCS registration date and a good-faith compliance narrative. Appeals of tax assessments must be filed within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Industry (Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale de l'industrie), via the Guichet.lu online application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment-permit application under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist, and certain liberal professions. Demonstrate the professional capacity and honourworthiness of the managers, adequate financial resources, and lawful premises. Because virtual card issuance is a regulated financial-sector activity, the application must expressly indicate the CSSF prudential licensing path for payment services/e-money (Stage 3) and confirm agreements with Mastercard and Visa Direct as the planned payment rails.
required_dossiers: Completed establishment-permit application form on guichet.lu
Curriculum vitae and professional qualification certificates of the gérants
Criminal record certificates from Luxembourg and any prior state of residence
Business plan, cash-flow projections, and proof of financial resources
Lease contract or ownership title for the registered office
Bank reference letter and evidence of the paid-up capital
Copy of any CSSF pre-notification acknowledgement received
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An establishment-permit refusal must be reasoned. The applicant may lodge an administrative appeal with the Minister of the Economy within two months and thereafter proceed before the administrative courts. Cure any identified gaps in managerial qualification, financial capacity, or premises documentation before resubmitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption, Fire Safety Clearance, and Occupational Health Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal fire prevention service with the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); building owner and registered-office landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formally adopt the registered office in Luxembourg City or another Grand-Duchy location through the board resolution and lease agreement. Obtain a fire-safety attestation (attestation de sécurité incendie) evidencing compliant escape routes, occupancy load, and fire-extinguishing equipment for office use. Notify the ITM of the establishment and prepare the workplace risk assessment. If card production, printing, or hardware vaulting is performed on site, verify electrical installations, structural floor load, and secure storage requirements; otherwise, confirm the activity is pure office-based.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or ownership deed for the registered office
Fire-safety attestation issued by the competent municipal authority
ITM establishment notification and workplace risk-assessment file
Floor plan and structural-load certificate where server rooms or vault storage are used
Public liability, property, and workplace insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire-safety authority requires corrective works, implement the listed measures and obtain a follow-up attestation before commencing card-issuing operations. ITM notices of non-compliance are appealable, but the safer cure is to implement the protective measures within the imposed timeline to avoid administrative fines under the Law of 17 June 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CSSF Prudential Pre-notification and Special Licensing Envelope (Stage 3 Gateway)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), 283 Route d'Arlon, L-1150 Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a preliminary notification and meeting request to the CSSF for authorisation as a payment institution or e-money institution under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended, and the Law of 10 November 2009 on e-money, as implemented by CSSF Circulars. Confirm fit-and-proper of the gérants, proof of own funds, the AML/CTF programme under the Law of 12 November 2004, and the intended payment-account and card-scheme arrangements with Mastercard and Visa Direct. This step is an information-gathering and pre-application clearance exercise; the formal authorisation application is the subject of Stage 3.
required_dossiers: Detailed programme of operations for virtual card issuance
Business plan covering card issuance, spend-management controls, and settlement flows
AML/CTF policy, KYC/KYB procedures, and transaction-monitoring framework
Fit-and-proper statements and criminal records of the gérants
Own-funds calculation and capital maintenance plan
Mastercard and Visa Direct network agreement drafts or letters of intent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSSF identifies completeness concerns, amend and resubmit the pre-notification dossier within the time limit indicated by the case officer. Schedule a pre-application meeting with the CSSF to align expectations. Material deficiencies in governance, capital, or AML controls must be cured before the Stage 3 full application is filed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Industry, in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for the regulated payment-institution and e-money authorisation required for virtual card issuing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011, together with the CSSF authorisation as a payment institution or e-money institution under the Laws of 10 November 2009 on payment services and on e-money, as amended

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity (Luxembourg Environmental Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA. Pure office-based virtual card issuance and spend-management operations do not fall within the Annexes of the Law of 22 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment. A simple prior notification may apply only if significant renovation of the registered office triggers the building-permit regime.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or point-source VOC emissions are generated. Compliance is required with the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management for office waste streams, the Grand-Ducal Regulation on waste electrical and electronic equipment, and the packaging waste provisions of EU Directive 94/62/EC as transposed. Any on-site destruction of plastic payment cards must follow classified waste handling codes and the EU waste framework directive; there is no applicable industrial discharge threshold for this office-based ISIC 6619 activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety attestation under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 February 2014 on fire prevention; structural-load and electrical-installation verification for the registered office; workplace risk assessment and ITM occupational clearance under the Law of 17 June 1994 on safety and health at work; public-liability and workplace insurance cover as a condition of the establishment permit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes; Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes; integrated electronic portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL must first complete incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the national registration number (matricule), which functions as the statutory tax identification number (TIN) for direct taxes, VAT, and social security. Where the SARL is owned by foreign persons or the entity is a foreign permanent establishment, the foreign parent must additionally register with the Luxembourg direct tax authorities using the Form 8 non-resident tax registration or similar, and file a VAT registration application (Form 1) with the AEDT when a taxable activity in Luxembourg is carried out. For non-established foreign entities, appointment of an approved VAT representative may be required; documentary proof includes constitutional documents, powers of attorney, evidence of place of effective management, and proof of the Luxembourg establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident Luxembourg SARL taxable on worldwide income; non-resident entities taxable only on Luxembourg-source income; SARL is subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime. Available elections include the VAT grouping election (assujetti unique), the corporate income tax fiscal unity election for resident entities held directly or indirectly at least 95%, and elections for certain ATAD hybrid mismatch adjustments. Certain Luxembourg-specific regimes such as the participation exemption and financial instruments provisions require timely election in the annual tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises; non-established foreign suppliers have no registration threshold and must register in Luxembourg when making taxable supplies there unless the reverse charge or EU place-of-supply rules shift the liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, stamping, or mandatory API-based approval of e-invoices. Electronic invoicing is mandatory in the B2G sector using PEPPOL/Factur-X templates; for B2B transactions, electronic invoices are freely issued without clearance if the recipient consents. Monthly and annual VAT returns, recapitulative statements (ECS), and Intrastat filings are submitted electronically through the AEDT portal. E-invoices must be retained in original form for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT if the supplier proves physical dispatch or transport outside EU territory within the legally prescribed period and retains transport/customs evidence. Cross-border B2B services to EU customers are reverse-charged to the customer; B2B services to non-EU customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (effectively zero-rated) where the customer receives the service at its non-EU establishment. Financial card-issuing and payment processing services in the scope of Article 135 VAT Directive are generally VAT-exempt without credit; export services of technical, electronic, or management nature require written customer declarations, contracts, and bank/payment records demonstrating the non-Luxembourg establishment of the recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (AES/DMS customs electronic declaration)
Transport Evidence (packing list, container tracking, delivery confirmation)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank Payment/SWIFT Evidence for settlement of the export sale
Written Customer Statement or Contract for non-EU service recipient status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg authorities may retrospectively assess VAT and claw back zero-rating benefits if export formalities or proof of physical export are deficient. The ordinary reassessment period is 5 years; in cases of intentional fraud, the period is 10 years. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims expose the taxpayer to default interest (0.6% monthly), fines of 50% to 100% of the evaded VAT, criminal penalties including imprisonment, and joint and several liability of statutory directors. Substantiation requires full chain of custody documents, bank settlement records, and contemporaneous transport evidence to survive audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank, with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the competent licensing and AML/CFT supervisory authority for payment institutions and e-money institutions, and the European Central Bank (ECB) for single monetary policy and TARGET2 oversight. Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration; capital-movement rules derive from EU Treaty Articles 63–65 and the amended Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and e-money.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full euro convertibility on both current and capital account. No exchange controls, no licensing of FX operations, and no restriction on dividend or profit remittance for the SARL. The only fiscal friction is the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (reduced to 0% for qualifying parent companies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or Luxembourg participation exemption, and minimised under tax treaties). Cash transfers out of Luxembourg are unrestricted provided Regulation (EU) 2015/847 (wire transfer information) and the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT are satisfied. No distinction between resident and non-resident accounts for convertibility purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to route export receipts through BCL. Corporate distribution and settlement receipts may be held freely in EUR or foreign currency. The residual compliance duty is statistical: the receiving bank files the BCL balance-of-payments declaration (ECB/BCL direct investment and services codes) for each qualifying cross-border transaction, and the SARL must maintain accurate back-up documentation for five years for CSSF and tax audit purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Settlement Account / Client-Funds Safeguarding Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Under the amended Law of 10 November 2009 and PSD2, an EU/EEA licensed EMI may provide accounts in Luxembourg through a passported branch or cross-border service, but a non-EU offshore digital EMI without substance cannot serve as the sole liquidity or safeguarding bank for the SARL because client card-funds must be safeguarded with a CSSF-licensed credit institution or equivalent. A licensed Luxembourg or passported EMI is acceptable for operational e-wallet functions only where it independently satisfies CSSF outsourcing and safeguarding requirements; unregulated offshore EMIs are contractually and legally unacceptable as the primary clearing bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for at least one director or authorised signatory at the bank's Luxembourg office for the first onboarding interview. Full remote opening is legally possible under CSSF AML/CFT rules if the bank operates a compliant e-KYC process using eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic identification or secure video-identification with notarised document verification, but tier-1 Luxembourg banks in practice require either (i) an in-person meeting with the compliance officer, or (ii) a certified identification at a Luxembourg notary or Luxembourg consulate, plus (iii) the original or certified copy of the SARL's RCS extract, the RBE UBO extract, and a board resolution on signatory authority. Where no director can travel, the standard fallback is a remote video conference combined with a notarial certificate of identity for each UBO and signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed payment-services activity: the SARL presents as a virtual-card issuer but cannot yet evidence a CSSF payment-institution (PI) or e-money-institution (EMI) authorisation, causing the bank to classify it as high-risk unregulated fintech.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF authorisation decision, or a dated and acknowledged CSSF authorisation application; a Luxembourg-qualified law firm legal opinion confirming the precise regulatory perimeter (PI vs EMI vs credit institution) and any available de-minimis or agent exemption; the Mastercard/Visa program-manager or sponsor-bank agreement; and the SARL's board-approved compliance implementation plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: nominee holdings, multi-tier non-EU ownership, or unreported ultimate beneficial owners above 25% create a statutory onboarding blocker under the amended Law of 12 November 2004.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE searchable extract; full shareholder register up to each natural-person UBO; chart of the ownership chain; passports and proof of residential address for each UBO; personal tax identification numbers; personal source-of-wealth records (employment certificates, historical bank statements, transaction, and dividend records); and notarised declarations of legitimate origin of funds for non-EU UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for the €12,000 subscribed share capital, shareholder loans, and pre-operational funding of card float.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) evidencing full subscription; blocked-account attestation (attestation de blocage de fonds) from the receiving bank; six months of bank statements and contract evidence for each contributing shareholder; auditor or certified accountant statement tracing the origin of each inward remittance; and the supporting loan agreements for any shareholder advance with arm's-length interest terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, fraud, and geographic concentration risk: virtual cards may be used for cross-border SaaS and media procuration in higher-risk jurisdictions, triggering enhanced due diligence on card acceptance geographies and merchants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy covering EU, UN, and OFAC lists; BIN-level and MCC-level geoblocking rules; real-time transaction-monitoring playbook; merchant and counterparty due diligence matrix with enhanced due diligence criteria for high-risk industries; certificates of no adverse sanctions hits for UBOs and counterparties; and a board attestation on restricted-coverage countries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client-money safeguarding and network settlement uncertainty: inability to demonstrate segregation of client funds before account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft or executed safeguarding agreement with the settlement bank providing a segregated client-money account per Article 30-32 of the amended Law of 10 November 2009; sponsor-bank settlement letter or draft network agreement from Mastercard and Visa confirming the settlement account scheme; independent auditor's report on the safeguarding process; and the CSSF reporting calendar for safeguarding verification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The statutory €12,000 minimum share capital and any additional shareholder pre-funding must be transferred by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's blocked capital account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance must carry the reference 'apport en capital – souscription d'actions SARL' together with the notary deed date and RCS file number, and the paying bank must transmit the full originator and beneficiary information required by Regulation (EU) 2015/847. The receiving bank will classify the transaction under the ECB/BCL balance-of-payments code for inward direct investment-equity capital for statistical reporting; funds remain frozen until the notarial deed is filed with the RCS. For intra-group shareholder loans above de-minimis, the bank requires the signed loan agreement, an interest-rate schedule, and a statement of the intended use to prevent Luxembourg thin-capitalisation recharacterisation. Capital can be received in any convertible currency without conversion obligation, although the bank may set a foreign-currency holding policy; the notary's attestation and the RBE extract must accompany the first draw.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EEA disbursements are executed via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for small-value flows and TARGET2/RTGS for high-value same-day settlements; non-EEA supplier payments are executed via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with the contracting party's IBAN/BIC and structured remittance fields. For high-value procurement of physical goods or regulated services, the SARL may use SWIFT MT700/MT710 documentary credits with the sponsor bank holding the commercial invoice, bill of lading, and certificate of origin; this is mandatory where the supplier requires payment-against-documentation. Card-network interchange is settled through the Mastercard/Visa clearing-and-settlement interface directly into the SARL's dedicated settlement account at the sponsor bank with D+1 net settlement and irrevocable clearing per network rules; any delay in funding the settlement account attracts a network chargeback and liquidity fine. Each outgoing transfer must be coded under the ECB/BCL services or investment code via the bank's reporting platform, and the SARL must retain the underlying invoice, purchase order, and delivery confirmation for five years for CSSF and tax audit purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot (T+2) for matching routine EUR/USD and EUR/GBP balances arising from card interchange and program fees
Outright FX forwards up to 12 months for hedging forecast card float and service-supplier exposures, documented under a board-approved treasury policy and ISDA 2002 Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through London or New York clearing desks for restricted currencies such as CNY, INR, KRW, and BRL where physical delivery is not legally possible; permitted only where the bank marks the transaction under the CSSF-compliant derivatives policy
FX swaps for short-term liquidity matching between the settlement-date funding requirement and the value date of incoming client card recharges
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term EUR/USD shareholder loan alignment, limited to plain-vanilla fixed-for-floating structures
Plain-vanilla European FX options and zero-premium collars where the bank has executed an ISDA credit support annex; exotic and leveraged FX derivatives are prohibited by board treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of RCS Registration Data (Confirmation Annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within one calendar month of the LBR electronic notification issued on the registration anniversary; the confirmation must be completed once per calendar year via the LBR e-file platform.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000 per non-compliant entity; repeating annual default for two successive years triggers ex officio dissolution proceedings and administrative strike-off from the RCS, followed by loss of corporate legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts and Statutory Audit Report Deposit (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing through the ePublication module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end). The accounts and audit report must first be approved by the ordinary general meeting within six months of year-end and be deposited no later than one month after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Filing default triggers procedural fines and adverse publication; failure to file for two consecutive financial years allows the Public Prosecutor or any interested third party to apply for judicial dissolution; managers may incur civil liability for resulting company losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owner Details (Confirmation Annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, within one calendar month of the LBR/RBE notification aligned with the registration anniversary; all shareholding transfers or changes in beneficial ownership must additionally be filed with the RBE within one month of the relevant corporate act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 per day of continued non-compliance imposed on legal representatives and directors; intentionally false declarations carry aggravated criminal penalties and civil liability to the company and third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting — Approval of Annual Accounts, Auditor Appointment and Discharge (AGM Minutes retained in the statutory Minute Book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record — shareholders' and managers' minutes held at the registered office; not deposited at the RCS unless judicial dissolution proceedings commence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each financial year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); the meeting must approve the annual accounts, decide on profit appropriation, and appoint/reelect the approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-observance of the six-month rule permits the Public Prosecutor to petition for judicial dissolution; in insolvency scenarios managers may be held personally liable for late filing and failure to maintain accurate corporate records.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is compulsory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds on its balance-sheet date under the amended Law of 19 December 2002: (i) balance-sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; (ii) net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,800,000; (iii) average workforce above 50 employees. In all cases a CSSF-regulated entity issuing corporate virtual cards under its payment-services or e-money licence must appoint a réviseur d'entreprises agréé regardless of whether the size thresholds are met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, as amended, transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the European Union is required for a licensed payment/e-money institution where imposed by the CSSF or group consolidation and may be applied voluntarily by the SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners, the SARL must file initial UBO details within one month of incorporation, update the RBE within one month of any shareholding transfer or control change, and confirm the registered UBO data annually through the LBR online portal upon anniversary-based notification; the confirmation attests that disclosed natural persons remain the ultimate beneficial owners and that transfer deeds are evidenced in the statutory share register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,300 – US$3,900 per annum (typical annual fee charged by Luxembourg registered-office/domiciliation agents)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$10,000 – US$35,000 per annum (typical certified audit fee range for a regulated fintech SARL, reflecting card transaction volumes and CSSF reporting scope)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City: 17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. Statutory reliefs: Luxembourg IP box exempts 80% of qualifying IP income, effective rate 4.94%; participation exemption exempts qualifying dividend and capital gain income; investment tax credit available for qualifying tangible/intangible assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official corporate income tax return: Modèle 100 / Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, filed electronically through the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) e-filing portal eCDF via MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year coinciding with the calendar year, the return is due no later than 31 December of the following calendar year when filed electronically; extensions may be granted by the tax office, and paper filing is subject to an earlier date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, tax matricule, RCS number, legal form SARL, Luxembourg VAT number, and authorised signatory details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg NIF and registered office; non-resident shareholders are not required to appear in the SARL CIT return; a permanent establishment of a foreign company would use a separate PE identification section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax per Luxembourg GAAP / IFRS annual accounts, including card issuance fees, interchange revenue, card program management fees, float income, and network expense deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg resident SARL must declare worldwide income; income attributable to a foreign PE is excluded only where a tax treaty grants an exemption or where the Luxembourg participation exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reversal of non-deductible items: fines, partial non-deductible entertainment expenses, excessive director remuneration paid to shareholders, hidden profit distributions, net wealth tax add-back where applicable, and ATAD-limited interest/royalty amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same treatment applies; non-resident shareholders cannot deduct costs attributable to their own foreign operations in the Luxembourg SARL return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of tax loss carry-forwards within the statutory carry-forward limit, participation exemption, Luxembourg IP box deduction (80% for qualifying IP), investment tax credits, and prior-year tax paid adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Luxembourg-resident taxpayer may apply Luxembourg reliefs; a foreign entity cannot claim Luxembourg loss carry-forwards unless it is subject to Luxembourg tax on a PE basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, CIT at 17%, solidarity surcharge at 7% of CIT, municipal business tax at the communal rate, available tax credits, and net tax payable after prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After calculating corporate tax, foreign income not attributable to Luxembourg is excluded where tax treaty relief applies; non-resident shareholders only face Luxembourg withholding tax at distribution stage, not in this box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative reminder, ex officio assessment, late-filing monetary penalties generally ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 5,000, and monthly late-payment surcharge equivalent to 0.6% per month plus 9% per annum statutory interest on unpaid tax. Deliberate false filing can result in criminal fines up to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15%; 0% for qualifying EU parent distributions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Luxembourg domestic participation exemption where the parent holds at least 10% or an acquisition price above EUR 1.2 million for at least 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit a valid certificate of tax residency (TRC), a beneficial ownership declaration, and evidence of qualifying shareholding and holding period to the Luxembourg paying agent before distribution or within the statutory refund window to the ACD. Excess withholding taxes are recovered through a Luxembourg tax refund claim or by direct treaty MAP if applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties is 0%. Most Luxembourg DTAs also preserve nil or nominal source taxation on royalties and interest; however, payments to related parties must satisfy the arm's length principle, substance requirements, and ATAD anti-abuse rules, otherwise the payments can be recharacterised as hidden dividends subject to 15% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 group consolidated revenue triggers CbC/Master File obligations; a Local File should be contemporaneously prepared for the SARL when the entity's related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 in a fiscal year, and is mandatory in practice where card scheme fee, technology licence, or treasury transactions exceed EUR 500,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate a formal ESR scorecard regime akin to UAE Economic Substance Regulations, but applies a substantive anti-abuse and substance doctrine through domestic GAAR, ATAD-transposed rules, DTA limitation-of-benefits clauses, DAC6, and the requirement that a société à responsabilité limitée have real local management, decision-making, staff, office premises, and operational control over card programme contracts, scheme management, settlement accounts, and treasury functions.
